correctness.rationale: Universal proof: every assignment of signs on the fifteen Hermitian two-qubit Paulis makes one of the six Peres–Mermin contexts inconsistent, because each of nine square entries occurs twice whereas the context-product signs multiply to -1. The rank-one joint (-rP,-rQ) projector on the inconsistent triple has exactly three expectations -r and other twelve zero; positivity forces (1-3gamma)/4 >= 0. The rank-one product projectors with local Bloch axes ±(1,1,1)/sqrt(3), mixed with weights (3±sqrt(3))/6, give all 15 expectations +1/3; convex interpolation with I/4 covers every 0<=gamma<=1/3 and is separable. Endpoint rank and purity are exact; W=sum P has bound 3 on the stabilizer polytope, while the constructed family has W=15gamma>3 for gamma>1/5. Direct exact small-matrix replay checks all 32768 sign assignments and the endpoint polynomial identity, but analytic proof rather than finite sampling gives state-space universality.

The claim here is precisely universal sharpness PLUS separable, nonstabilizer attainment for the whole indicated interval, using the classical Peres–Mermin square as acknowledged input. Targeted published-finding corpus and primary-literature comparisons found no direct prior theorem of this strength. value.rationale: An equal-modulus full two-qubit Pauli spectrum is a natural quantum-information invariant motivated by WH-SIC and magic state research. The theorem determines the exact feasible contrast set for all mixed two-qubit states, proves a sign-universal obstruction using a contextuality geometry, and shows that the sharp endpoint and nonstabilizer witnesses are realized by separable rank-two mixtures. Thus maximal flat Pauli correlations and nonstabilizer character need not entail bipartite entanglement. It is a structural exact classification, not arbitrary numerical slicing, while making no claim about computation advantage or larger systems.
